text.p: Following are politicians comments after first round French parliamentary election results showed the combined left leading the centre-right.
This is not a good result for the current majority. It is a warning shot. It shows some disappointment, irritation, discontent...It will have to be taken into account before the second round.
LAURENT FABIUS, FORMER SOCIALIST PRIME MINISTER

This is a strong rejection of government policy. It think that we have all felt during this camapign the expression of a strong will for change...For the left, it's satisfactory. We will not fall into triumphalism because there is a second round...A change is possible, this evening is perhaps the start of a new hope.

The certainty is that the French wanted to send a warning to the government but they don't want a return to the past. The many partisans of the majority who abstained or who spread their votes in the first round will this week mobilise to reaffirm their choice of team for the second round.
NICOLAS SARKOZY, FORMER BUDGET MINISTER (RPR PARTY)

You cannot deny these results. I would have liked them to be better. But can the Socialists be happy about these results? The outcome of the vote will be very indecisive, very difficult. We have to explain better what will change on the style of government and the programme to be put in place.
BRUNO MEGRET, DEPUTY LEADER OF THE NATIONAL FRONT

This is a pretty lashing rejection for those who dissolved the National Assembly. It's also an unenthusiastic push for the left, and a very positive result for the National Front...an absolute record that exceeds the score of Jean-Marie Le Pen in the 1995 presidential race.
Asked who he would recommend his supporters to back on the second round, he said: "Candidates of the National Front"
